item.title: Giants release WR Darius Slayton
item.description: The NY Giants part with their longest-tenured veteran
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants announced that they have released veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton.

Slayton, 29, was drafted by the Giants in the fifth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and was, up until his release, the longest tenured Giant on the roster.

The Giants create just $3.16 million in cap space while taking on $12.75 million in dead cap money by releasing Slayton.

Slayton made an immediate impact for the Giants as a rookie. His uncommon blend of size and speed made him a much-needed deep threat, and he quickly built a strong rapport with fellow 2019 draftee, QB Daniel Jones. While Slayton never cracked 800 yards receiving, he did eclipse 700 yards in four of his first five seasons (2019, 2020, 2022, and 2023). He led the Giants in receiving in each of those seasons.

That said, while Slayton provided a much-needed vertical element to the Giants’ offense, he has struggled to consistently generate separation with his route running. He has also struggled with drops throughout his career.

All told, Slayton has played in 106 games for the Giants, starting 78. He has 296 catches for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns as a Giant. Despite his limitations, Slayton was an undeniable hit as a fifth round pick.

The release of Slayton positions Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields to be primary receivers along with Malik Nabers and Odell Beckham Jr.

It remains to be seen how the Giants will fill the roster hole created by releasing Slayton. They could sign Braxton Berrios to their active roster, or they could add a free agent and keep their trio of returners on the practice squad.

item.title: Mike LaFleur says he feels "good" about Jeremiyah Love's chances for Week 1
item.description: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders. It was diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain, and he has not practiced or played since.

Love is moving closer to a return, though, and coach Mike LaFleur insinuated that the rookie did something on the practice field Monday.

"Progressing," LaFleur said, via Bo Brack of PHNX Cardinals. "He was out there moving around today. We'll see on Wednesday. I'll have a better idea for all those guys [who are injured]."

The Cardinals will have their first injury report of the season on Wednesday, which will be the first indication of where Love is in his rehab. LaFleur was asked about his optimism for the third overall pick to play against the Chargers.

"Yeah, I feel good," LaFleur said.

Love had 14 touches for 73 yards in the first half of the only preseason game he played.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan disappointed that NFL took away ‘home game in LA’ for Australia game
item.description: The Niners will miss out on home game opportunity in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
When it was announced that the San Francisco 49ers were playing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, one of the biggest detractors was head coach Kyle Shanahan, who expressed his displeasure with the travel and setup.

Having landed in Australia and now preparing for the Week 1 game this week, has his mind changed about the situation?

“When I said that, that was nothing against Australia or anything,” Shanahan said on Sunday. “That’s just about competition and how important our 17 games are. It’s cool for us, just we always have an advantage of having one, I see it as one home game a year in L.A. Just the way our fans are and take over that stadium.”

The 49ers do generally get that extra home game, forcing the Rams into silent counts at their own home stadium. So, there are certain years where San Francisco could get their nine original home games plus that extra game.

This season, San Francisco has eight home games and nine road contests, with the Australia game counting as a road game. So, they won’t have an extra appearance at SoFi Stadium (although they do face the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi in December).

But the 49ers fanbase does travel well, so Week 1 could be a similar environment anyway.

“It was disappointing to let them off the hook and get them out of that,” Shanahan continued. “But, I have a feeling knowing how our fans roll, I have a feeling they won’t be much different here. I expect to have a good showing. I wouldn’t say it hit me right on the plane, but after being here for a couple of days, this is the right time to be here, it’s the right place to be, and it’s the right team to go against.”

If there were a week for an international game, Week 1 is the most ideal, as teams can prepare for it beforehand, whereas they have to adjust on the fly in-season. That’s why the Rams approach is quite unique, as they’re essentially preparing like it’s in-season with their flights.

After getting a few days to adjust, Shanahan is happy that the team went with their approach.

“Not comparing us to them, but yeah I was glad. I know how I felt the last couple, two days. It’s a little different for a coach, toughing through how you use your mind for three-and-a-half hours, a little bit different than your body. But yeah, I’m glad that we’ve been out here because we feel real good today.”

San Francisco and Los Angeles kick off on Friday morning local time, but the game will be aired on Netflix at 5:35 p.m. Pacific time on Thursday evening.

item.title: What will the NFL standings look like in 2026?
item.description: How will the heavily favored Rams finish in the NFC after falling short of the Super Bowl?
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams are heavily favored to win the Super Bowl in February and came out nicely in these NFL standings predictions for the 2026 season. However, that’s not all when looking ahead to the season, which starts with a Seahawks-Patriots title rematch on Wednesday.

Plenty of other surprises are in store in these projections, including where the Cowboys and Bengals finish after defensive overalls, who the actual worst team in the NFL is and potential upheaval in the NFC North.

It’s time to dive into some NFL regular season standings predictions to see what the Rams will be up against. Turf Show Ramily, I’d also love to see any predictions you have — or to tell me how full of it I am — in the comments. Let’s do this!

AFC East

Bills (12-5)

Patriots (11-6)

Dolphins (4-13)

Jets(4-13)

The Bills whiffed on their last best chance to make a Super Bowl run in 2025, with the Chiefs and Ravens missing the playoffs. Not much should change in Buffalo, even with a new coach in the fold. Josh Allen is still incredible and should compete for MVP honors. He’s the glue keeping that team together. Overall, the Bills are a well-rounded team that will be good enough to lose to KC for the umpteenth time. New England, coming off an AFC title, is a good team that benefited from a painfully easy schedule and a lucky string of playoff opponents to get to the Super Bowl. The Patriots will be a major player in the conference again. A.J. Brown will be a downgrade in the offense after letting Stefon Diggs walk, though. He wasn’t great towards the end of his time in Philly. Guess we’ll see what chemistry he really has with Drake Maye.

The Dolphins and Jets are lumped into one since they’ll both be awful. I anticipate the Jets will actually be the worst team in the division, with Miami coming out just ahead. Congrats? Now, the Dolphins have the worst roster, while New York has the worst coaching staff, and that will make the difference. Aaron Glenn is a terrible head coach and might be the first coach fired when his team’s season inevitably goes south. Either way, both directionless franchises are trapped in a top-heavy division. Not ideal.

AFC North

Ravens (12-5)

Bengals(10-7)

Steelers(8-9)

Browns (4-13)

The Ravens had a lot of bad luck in 2025, yet things should be better under new coach Jesse Minter. Lamar Jackson is one of the league’s best quarterbacks and will return to his MVP ways under the new leadership. Baltimore has a painfully easy start to the year, which could help boost their chances at the AFC’s top seed later in the season. The Bengals have the most experienced coach in the division, something not brag-worthy in the slightest, but could help them in the long run. Much of Cincy’s success will hinge on two things: Joe Burrow’s health and the defense. An average defense will get them back to the playoffs. Let their powerful offense do the rest.

Pittsburgh should’ve pulled the trigger on a full rebuild the second Mike Tomlin stepped down. The Steelers are too old and don’t resemble a playoff team. Though, with all their big names, this team would’ve kicked ass five years ago. Mike McCarthy was such an uninspired hire for them. They had a chance to hop on the trend of young offensive minds and instead chose a dinosaur. McCarthy is a good coach, just not what the Steelers needed. Also, Aaron Rodgers and McCarthy didn’t work towards the end of their time in Green Bay, so no one should expect the sequel to go any differently.

Even without Myles Garrett, the Browns should be set on defense. They have to be good since their quarterback situation is so putrid. No matter who starts under center won’t matter. This is a poverty franchise whose owners made a stupid call in naming Deshaun Watson the starter. Oh, you thought the coaching staff made that call? Man, it must be nice to be that naive.

AFC South

Texans (11-6)

Jaguars(10-7)

Colts(7-10)

Titans(5-12)

Houston might have a problem at the quarterback spot if CJ Stroud continues his decline. However, that defense will keep them in every game this season. Everyone wants to give the Rams and Seahawks the nod for the best defense, but the Texans are most deserving of that title. Their red-hot finish last season after a sluggish start will carry over as they reclaim the NFC South.

Jacksonville should again be a playoff fixture under second-year coach Liam Coen. Trevor Lawrence hasn’t been anything special in the NFL despite flashes, yet he came into his own under Coen throughout the second half of the season.

His progression will be something to monitor as the Jaguars look to make a deep playoff run. The Colts are all aboard the hot mess express. Indianapolis will do enough to remain in the playoff hunt until the final month of the season. I’m not expecting Daniel Jones to build on what he began there, so expect the Colts to be in the QB market again next offseason.

Don’t be surprised if Tennessee fields a top 10 defense this season. Robert Saleh is an excellent defensive-minded coach, which the Titans will need since Cam Ward apparently can’t hit the broad side of a barn. Saleh will need the best coaching job of his career if his new team hopes to go anywhere, or else it’ll be his Jets tenure all over again.

AFC West

Broncos(12-5)

Chiefs (10-7)

Chargers (10-7)

Raiders(6-11)

The Broncos surprised many people last year en route to earning the AFC’s top seed. Denver won’t have that luxury in 2026, yet they have a top five roster in the sport. Bo Nix will certainly enjoy throwing to new target Jaylen Waddle, and Sean Payton handing off playcalling duties might be the jumpstart the offense needed. The defense will also be chasing an NFL single-season sack record after finishing with 68 last season. They’ll remain the class of a weak conference, even if their win total dips slightly.

With Patrick Mahomes back, the Chiefs should return to playoff contention after an off year. Kansas City lost many pieces via trade and free agency, including a couple to the Rams in Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Even though they’re not a player in the Super Bowl picture, count out Mahomes and Andy Reid at your own risk.

The Chargers are a middling AFC team that’s only relevant because they play in a weak conference. Los Angeles has been outclassed in back-to-back playoff appearances under Jim Harbaugh, and not much should change this season. They’ll be good enough to make the playoffs, but nothing more, which is the story of their team under Harbaugh. Las Vegas should be much improved after moving on quickly from the disastrous Pete Carroll era, even if that’s not well reflected in the win column. First-year coach Klint Kubiak has several young playmakers to work with, like Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders will be a handful for opposing defenses.

NFC East

Cowboys (10-7)

Eagles(10-7)

Giants(7-10)

Commanders(6-11)

America’s Team (barf) will win the NFC East in 2026. How’s that for spicy? The Cowboys have had a solid offseason and have done enough to overtake the Eagles, at least this season. They’ve added plenty of nice pieces to improve their horrid defense from a year ago. Dallas can move the ball with ease, and like the Bengals, an average D will get them back into the playoffs.

Philadelphia is in a strange spot. They have one of the league’s best rosters and should be a title threat, yet they keep getting in their own way. Vic Fangio is still there, so the defense will remain elite. Sean Mannion was an interesting choice at offensive coordinator. Former Packers coaches haven’t typically fared well in new locations: see Luke Getsy and Nathaniel Hackett.

New York has plenty of young talent who should come together quite nicely for new coach John Harbaugh. The Giants are likely a year away from competing for the playoffs. Jaxson Dart has plenty to prove in his second season, namely that he can make good decisions both on and off the field, and not follow the playing style of his dunderhead teammate, Cam Skattebo. Washington should be better this season, but only if a lot of things go right. Dan Quinn and Jayden Daniels will be under the microscope a lot as the Commanders seek a return to the playoffs after a one-year absence.

NFC North

Lions (11-6)

Bears(10-7)

Packers(8-9)

Vikings (6-11)

The NFC North is back to being the black-and-blue division after every team finished above .500 for the second time ever in the 17-game era. Detroit finished fourth in the division a year ago and is one of the most popular worst-to-first candidates in the NFL this season. The Lions are playing a last place schedule and have retained much of the core talent that has brought them back to relevance under head coach Dan Campbell. It’s unlikely the division will have everyone finish with a winning record for a second year in a row, and even less likely that the North will have multiple playoff teams in a loaded NFC. Detroit is my pick to win it.

As for the rest of the division, the Bears are the biggest regression candidate in the league after winning several nail-biters in 2025. They’ll have a tougher time winning those types of games this season, but they should still be a quality team. It all rides on Caleb Williams, who has been the toast of Chicago, but will he keep it up? Da Bears should have a top 10 offense, which they’ll need because their defense will likely stink again.

I was going to slot the Packers in last place until I remembered the Vikings exist — more on them in a moment. Green Bay has collapsed late in the year the last two seasons, which is a sign of who they are, rather than a trend. They haven’t had the best offseason and don’t have anyone to step up with Micah Parsons set to miss a chunk of time. Plus, questions remain about whether Jordan Love is the guy. We already know Matt LaFleur isn’t. Have some cheese curds ready, as Packers fans will need them to drown their sorrows this season.

The Vikings should be a Super Bowl contender if they could ever figure out the quarterback spot. Kyler Murray isn’t the answer. He clearly wasn’t for the Cardinals, so why would Minnesota expect anything to change now? Wow, J.J. McCarthy must really stink that bad, huh? Defensively, they’re in a good spot, but things will get ugly real quick if the Vikings cannot figure things out. Kevin O’Connell will be the scapegoat should that happen.

NFC South

Panthers(8-9)

Saints (8-9)

Buccaneers(7-10)

Falcons (7-10)

The NFC South is a disgrace of a division, so I’m not about to waste much time discussing it. Carolina won it last year with a losing record and will do the same in 2026. They’re the best of the trash and will be rewarded with a home playoff game, because why the hell not? It’s only fair, isn’t it? New Orleans could be a fun team if Kellen Moore can get things figured out in his second season. They’ll be a player for the division crown since the South is that weak. Tampa Bay lost seven of eight following a 6-2 start, and won’t be much better this time around. How Todd Bowles has a job is beyond me, so Baker Mayfield might be left to carry this team the best he can again. And the Falcons? Two words: Tua Tagovailoa. LOL.

Since 2022, the division has been won by a team that finished with single-digit win totals, including twice with a losing record. Yeah, no one should overlook anyone in the NFL, but I’ll make an exception here. This division isn’t worth being taken seriously. Now, on to the REAL football teams.

NFC West

Rams (14-3)

Seahawks(12-5)

49ers(9-8)

Cardinals (3-14)

The Rams are the easy division and Super Bowl pick, simply because they are the best team … on paper. That’s not simply me being a biased Rams writer either. LA has far and away the best roster, and not much should realistically get in their way, besides things like the injury bug and their own lofty expectations. They are built like a dream Madden team, yet sometimes, all it takes is one bad game to derail everything. The front offense has done all it possibly could, and it might not be done come trade deadline time.

Don’t sleep on Seattle. Don’t you dare do it, you dumb dumbs. It sometimes feels like too many around the league have, as the Rams have been getting the bulk of the headlines. I’m sorry, but did LA dominate on their way to winning the Super Bowl last season? Yeah, didn’t think so. The Seahawks are a title contender, despite losing several pieces this offseason. They’re the true team to beat until proven otherwise.

San Francisco has had a hectic offseason, and that noise will likely carry over into the regular season. Injuries are always a concern in the Bay Area and should be again. The 49ers were fortunate to get as far as they did in ‘25 given all the injuries they had. They won’t be as fortunate this time around, but will remain a wild card threat. And hey, if the injuries get too out of hand, they can give that Daejon Love a call.

Poor Arizona. They’re in a division with three playoff contenders and are so far away from competing with each of them. The Cardinals will be a bad, bad team, but might be able to move the ball under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. Still, they’ll be the NFL’s worst team, and who knows when they’ll get out of this cycle of suck.

item.title: Colts seek to start new streak after slaying old one
item.description: The Colts need to start a new streak.
item.content:encoded:
Opening week in the NFL is special. After a long offseason, the beginning of a new season brings renewed hope and excitement. Although not always the end of the world, one way to dampen that joy is to lose Week One. The Indianapolis Colts put on a master class of that by going winless since 2013. That decade-plus streak was painful, but it was sweet release when they finally ended the futility by beating the Dolphins last year. With one streak over, the Colts are looking to start a new one. 

The Dolphins were bad last year. No one knew how bad when the Colts beat the absolute brakes off them, but then again, the Colts were world beaters to start the season. They will have to regain that form if they are going to win against the Ravens. 

There are a few advantages working in the Colts’ favor. Being at home is always a benefit. It hasn’t always translated into wins but a home game to start the season is more palatable than a road contest. The Colts also have decent health. Some players have dings, but they should be close to full go. Daniel Jones is ready and has an offseason under his belt with the team. 

The Ravens will prove to be a formidable opening opponent. Lamar Jackson is one of the best in the game. His elusiveness will be a challenge for the Colts to contain. Early projections have the Ravens winning 10-11 games with 9 out of 10 fans feeling optimistic about the season. Winning the AFC North is the target which means they don’t plan on faltering against the Colts. 

The Colts broke their Week One curse. Now is the time to start a new streak. It won’t be easy, but why should it be? If the Colts can win against the Ravens, it would prove to be a fantastic measuring stick. It would be an early feather in their cap. Let a new streak begin!

item.title: NFL news, live updates: Falcons name Tua Tagovailoa their starter; Christian McCaffrey, Nick Bosa not spotted at practice
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news and injury updates approaching Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to NFL kickoff week, as we await the much-anticipated season opener between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday — a rematch of Super Bowl LX.

Kicking off the news cycle ahead of Week 1 was word from the Atlanta Falcons that Tua Tagovailoa had been named the starting quarterback over Michael Penix Jr. for Week 1's season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tagovailoa had just about every opportunity to win the job while Penix recovered from an ACL injury that ended his 2025 campaign, but had a shaky performance in training camp and the preseason, likely leaving the door open for Penix to re-take the job.

Fans will also be keeping an eye on the injury status of several stars ahead of Week 1, including San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey and pass rusher Nick Bosa, as well as New England Patriots second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson — all of whom are dealing with bumps and bruises on a short week leading up to their teams’ season openers.

item.title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins return to Bengals practice
item.description: The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1.

Chase and Higgins returned to practice on Monday. Chase hyperextended his knee in a practice and Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion. Defensive end Shemar Stewart also practiced after returning to the field from a knee injury last week and head coach Zac Taylor made it sound like all three are on track to play.

"All three looked good today," Taylor said at his press conference. "We'll wait to release injury reports on Wednesday, but I was encouraged by the progress all three of those guys have made."

The Bengals would like to get off to a fast start this season and having all three players on the field against the Bucs would be a good step in that direction.

item.title: Newcomer Zaire Franklin named a Packers captain, along with four repeat captains from 2025
item.description: It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader.
item.content:encoded:
It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader.

Franklin, who arrived in Green Bay via a trade in March, has been named one of the Packers' captains. That's not a surprise, as Franklin was a team captain on the Colts in each of the last six seasons. Some players exude leadership, and Franklin is one of them.

The Packers named five captains, Franklin and four players who were also Packers captains last year: quarterback Jordan Love, tight end Tucker Kraft, safety Xavier McKinney and special teamer Isaiah McDuffie.

Three players who were Packers team captains last year are not captains this year: Rashan Gary and Quay Walker, who are no longer in Green Bay, and Josh Jacobs, who is currently on the commissioner's exempt list amid an investigation into an accusation of violence against a woman.

item.title: Patrick Paul, Aaron Brewer bullish on Kadyn Proctor’s Dolphins debut
item.description: “He’s been ready,” said Paul.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins will be playing football on Sunday in Las Vegas against the Raiders. Not preseason football, not exhibition football, but real-life, regular season NFL football. As such, their starting left guard — rookie Kadyn Proctor — will be making his National Football League debut.

When the Dolphins traded out of selecting safety Caleb Downs and bypassed adding EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft to instead select Proctor out of Alabama, the internet exploded with consternation over the selection. But, Miami’s new general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, targeted the big lineman for a reason — he wants Miami to be tougher and more physical at the point of attack on offense, and not just reliant on smoke and mirrors like past regimes succeeded with. He also wanted his big investment — quarterback Malik Willis — to be protected at all costs.

Throughout the summer, many Dolphins fans continued to bemoan the Proctor selection — but those in the buildings in Miami Gardens are instead singing his praises.

Dolphins veteran center Aaron Brewer met with the South Florida media following Monday’s practice and was asked about Proctor’s potential and what makes the young player special. “His size. His speed. That’s an athletic big dude,” said Brewer.

Miami’s third-year left tackle, Patrick Paul, also had good things to say about Miami’s starting left guard. “He’s been ready. He’s ready. He’s a different kind of rookie,” spoke Paul of Proctor.

The words have been spoken. Now it’s time for Proctor to quiet the lips of his doubters with action. He’ll get that opportunity on Sunday when the Dolphins take on the Raiders in the late afternoon window of the inaugural NFL Sunday of the 2026 season.

item.title: Raiders Week 1: The must-account-for Dolphins in the home opener
item.description: Miami running back De’Von Achane, linebacker Jordyn Brook can take over and dominate a game if Las Vegas isn’t on point
item.content:encoded:
It might’ve just been me, but it sure felt like it took a while for us to get into Week 1 mode, but alas, here we are and the Las Vegas Raiders are set to embark on the regular season with Klint Kubiak as their head coach.

The Silver & Black kick off its 2026 campaign by hosting the Miami Dolphins inside Allegiant Stadium this Sunday afternoon. And the battle between the AFC West and AFC East squads features a clash between two rookie head coaches — Kubiak and Jeff Hafley — in charge of rebuilding squads.

Much like the Raiders did two offseason ago with cleaning house and hiring John Spytek in January of 2025 and two days later inking one-and-done head coach Pete Carroll (which ushered the Kubiak era the following offseason), the Dolphins pressure washed its front office and coaching staff with the additions of GM Jon-Eric Sullivan and Hafley (a pair of Green Bay Packers with the former serving as vice president of player personnel and the latter as defensive coordinator).

But as the case was in Las Vegas, Miami’s roster cupboard is far from barren.

The team has intriguing elite talent — even after the Dolphins did the customary roster purge that often accompanies a new primary personnel man and head coach. And Kubiak and Co. must account for them as running back De’Von Achane has the explosiveness, speed, and versatility to make even the best NFL defenses look foolish while linebacker Jordyn Brooks is a smart and hard-hitting linebacker that can ruin an NFL offense’s best laid plans.

Achane Attack

The 24-year-old running back produced a career-best 1,350 yards on 238 carries last season for Miami. Standing 5-foot-9 and 195 pounds, the third-round pick (84th overall) from the 2023 NFL Draft exceeded expectations coming out of Texas A&M. Adding four more end zone trips as a receiver, that 12-touchdown performance in 2025 set as new career-high mark.

He’s every bit as fast as the 4.32-second 40-yard dash time he clocked a the NFL Combine and the eight rushing touchdowns he had this past season tied the same number he had as a rookie in 2023.

By The Numbers
De’Von Achane, Running Back, 4th Year

  • 2025: 16 games (all starts), 238 carries, 1,350 yards, 8 touchdowns; 85 targets, 67 receptions, 488 yards, 4 touchdowns
  • Career: 44 games (36 starts), 544 carries, 3,057 yards, 22 touchdowns; 209 targets, 172 receptions, 1,277 yards, 13 touchdowns

The matchup between Achane and the Raiders’ defense puts the unsettled interior run defense under the microscope and spotlight in Week 1. Late-camp addition Folorunso Fatukasi (6-foot-4, 318 pounds, 31 years old) impressed Las Vegas to make the 53-man roster and his fellow defensive tackles — Thomas Booker IV, Adam Butler, Jonah Laulu, Tonka Hemingway, and JJ Pegues — will have their hands full (depending on how his active gameday). That group up front must control the line of scrimmage along with the A and B gaps to allow linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker to make plays alongside Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye on the edges.

Achane is the type to truly test the Raiders defense as one mistake, one missed assignment can result in the tailback finding the end zone either from the interior or perimeter. And we’ll get to see if Crosby and Paye — players who can rack up tackles for loss defending the run — can get the job done.

Defenders charged with covering Achane out of the backfield as a receiver presents equal headaches and if he gets going, it can limit the Raiders defense from pass rush opportunities against Miami quarterback Malik Willis, who has the athleticism to scramble and run around, himself.

The Week 1 matchup entails seeing Leonard’s full gamut defense as opposed to the vanilla play calls he ran during preseason. And that should be intriguing to see how it’ll play out.

By The Brooks

The success of Kubiak’s offense is often predicated on the run and what a great test for the Raiders by battling against Brooks.

The centerpiece of Hafley’s defense, the 28-year-old Texas Tech product packs a mean wallop in his 6-foot and 240-pound frame. With solid size, speed (4.54-second 40-yard dash time in the 2020 NFL Combine), and exceptional football intelligence, Brooks is the epitome of a sideline-to-sideline linebacker that can blow up stretch or outside zones before the blocking develops. He’s also a downhill punisher who can eradicate gap and power runs, too, which earned him first-team NFL All Pro honors in 2025.

By The Numbers
Jordyn Brooks, Linebacker, 7th Year

  • 2025: 17 games (all starts), 183 total tackles (99 solo), 13 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 3 pass deflections, 1 forced fumble, 1 fumble recovery
  • Career: 97 games (89 starts), 839 total tackles (494 solo), 47 tackles for loss, 13 sacks, 1 interception, 25 pass deflections, 3 forced fumbles, 6 fumble recoveries

Kubiak did well to bring in a fullback to provide the hardnosed lead blocker for his running backs — be it Ashton Jeanty or scintillating rookie Mike Washington Jr. — and the eventual meeting between Connor Heyward and Brooks will be one to watch. Brooks ability to diagnose run plays quickly alongside his size and speed allows the linebacker to truly blow up downhill blocking schemes.

Brooks has the instincts and movement skills to be a nuisance in the middle of the field as a cover man — although this is the weakest aspect of his game as Pro Football Reference charted him with allowing 66 receptions on 86 targets (76.7 completion percentage allowed) for 665 yards and three touchdowns last season.

With Kubiak’s penchant to run multiple tight end sets, testing Brooks’ coverage chop opens with both Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer and running backs coming out of the backfield is a must-do.

item.title: Steelers will not have season-long captains under Mike McCarthy
item.description: The Steelers’ head coach unveiled a new way of naming team captains in Monday’s press conference.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday will mark the official start of a new era of Pittsburgh Steelers football as Mike McCarthy will make his regular season debut as the head coach of the team he grew up rooting for. It will be the first time since 2007 that a new man will be in charge of the Steelers for their season opener. With that will come a number of changes to the way the team handles business.

One of those things this season will be the way in which the team names captains. When asked about how the team would select captains in Monday’s press conference, McCarthy provided some details into the changes coming to that selection process this fall.

“We’ll do the weekly captain format,” McCarthy told the media. “So, without getting ahead of myself here, when we get to that point in that week I’ll get that information to you.”

Under former head coach Mike Tomlin, captains were named in the preseason and stayed the same throughout the duration of the season. Now, no single player will have the right to be a captain all season long.

This is not an entirely new concept for McCarthy, as he took a similar approach to naming weekly captains during his time as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. Now, he brings a fresh captain-choosing philosophy to his hometown.

Last season, Aaron Rodgers, Cam Heyward, and Miles Killebrew were named captains before the start of the season. After Killebrew suffered a season-ending injury, it was linebacker Payton Wilson who took over as the special teams captain.

It would not be surprising to see veterans like Rodgers and Heyward earn the weekly captain title several times throughout the season, but now younger players will be incentivized for their efforts by potentially earning the title of weekly captain.

item.title: Dan Quinn: Full participation in practice today; trending in right direction for Week 1
item.description: Dan Quinn gives updates on Week 1 in his first “Tell the Truth” Monday of the season
item.content:encoded:
Dan Quinn is back for his weekly “Tell the Truth Mondays” as the team begins their official Week 1 preparations. The season opener is in Philadelphia this year, and they’re visiting last season’s NFC East Champion Eagles. They are big underdogs, and follow that up with another road division game against the Cowboys. Quinn said everyone participated in practice today, including OLB Odafe Oweh who is dealing with a calf injury. Today was only a walkthrough, but Quinn said everyone is trending towards being available for Week 1.

Quinn likes the energy he’s seen from the team so far, and also the leadership. He named five season-long captains, a change from the weekly captains he’s done the previous years. He will still name one additional captain weekly, but Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin, Frankie Luvu, Jeremy Reaves, and Tress Way are clear leaders in the locker room. Daniels only played one series in the preseason again, but Quinn insisted that he has gotten more reps in training camp and during joint practices that prepared him for his third season in the NFL. Training camp has been more intense than Quinn’s first two in Washington, another part of the plan to not have a repeat of last year’s disappointing 5-12 record.

item.title: Cowboys LG Tyler Smith to undergo thumb surgery, expected to miss 4-6 weeks
item.description: Smith has dealt with a ligament issue in his thumb for some time, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith will undergo thumb surgery and be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday.

As a result, the three-time Pro Bowler will be placed on injured reserve. The injury is to a ligament in Smith's thumb and had been bothering the fifth-year veteran for some time, according to Schottenheimer.

After attempting to play with the issue, no improvement was apparent and Smith's grip strength was affected. Thus, the decision was made to undergo surgery, which will occur on Tuesday.

Cowboys All-Pro LG Tyler Smith is going to have thumb surgery. Sounds like he will be out 4-6 weeks. TJ Bass will start in his place

— Jon Machota (@jonmachota) September 7, 2026

Fourth-year guard T.J. Bass will replace Smith. He appeared in 16 games last season with five starts.

"At the end of the day, he felt like he couldn't do things he to do at a high level," Schottenheimer said, via The Athletic's Jon Machota. "This is a long season, so let's go get it fixed.

It's unfortunate, but that's why we coveted T.J. Bass," he added. "He's played a lot of really good football for us and we expect he will continue to do so."

Despite Smith's absence, the Cowboys are still expected to have one of the top offensive lines in the NFL with center Cooper Beebe and right guard Tyler Booker on the interior, and Tyler Guyton at left tackle and Terence Steele on the right. Recently acquired Broderick Jones is competing with Steele for that right tackle position.

Last season, that line helped Dallas accumulate 6,663 yards, the second-highest total in the league.

Smith, 25, has started 63 games for Dallas during the past four seasons. He played 98% of the team's offensive snaps when he was in the lineup. Last season, he was flagged for seven penalties (three times for holding).

The 6-foot-5, 328-pounder was the Cowboys' 2022 first-round pick (No. 24 overall) out of Tulsa.

item.title: Detroit Lions make several roster moves ahead of Week 1 vs. Saints
item.description: The Detroit Lions have filled 1 of 2 roster vacancies after a plethora of roster moves on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions have made a few more roster maneuvers to get the roster ready for their Week 1 matchup with the New Orleans Saints. Detroit started the week with two vacancies on their 53-man roster. Now they’ll still have one.

Detroit announced that:

  • Linebacker Joe Bachie has signed from the practice squad to the 53-man roster
  • C Seth McLaughlin has signed to the practice squad
  • RB Jabari Small has signed to the practice squad
  • G Mason Miller has been placed on the practice squad injured reserve list

Starting with Bachie, he takes up a spot on the 53-man roster now, giving Detroit an extra body amongst a crowded linebacker room. But with rookie Jimmy Rolder missing most of training camp and not officially back yet, Detroit likely needed someone who can provide depth on gameday and play special teams. Bachie is a six-year veteran with seven career starts and over 1,100 special teams snaps.

McLaughlin and Small’s return to the practice squad was expected. Both players made the team’s initial 53-man roster, but were waived later in the week in order to do some roster maneuvering. It would not be surprising to see McLaughlin get a Week 1 practice squad elevation considering Detroit currently doesn’t have a healthy backup center behind Juice Scruggs. Small could also provide some gameday depth, but it sounds like the Lions already have other RB2 plans with Isiah Pacheco starting the season on injured reserve.

Speaking of IR, it’s a disappointment to see Miller land on the practice squad IR. He was a great story on the final week of training camp, because he had to be the team’s emergency center during the final preseason game and played quite well despite no experience at the position. Unfortunately, he’ll be sidelined for at least four games. Like on the active roster IR, Miller will not count against the team’s practice squad 16-player maximum capacity.

Detroit still has an empty spot on the 53-man roster. Smart money is on wide receiver Tom Kennedy to assume that spot, but the Lions may be waiting until next week to do so, because his contract would become fully guaranteed if he were on the Week 1 roster. Regardless, Kennedy is likely to be a part of Sunday’s roster, as he’s the leading candidate to be the team’s starting punt returner and fourth or fifth wide receiver.

item.title: Cowboys lose star offensive lineman to injury days before season opener
item.description: With the 2026 NFL season around the corner, the Cowboys were dealt a blow as Tyler Smith will land on injured reserve.
item.content:encoded:
It's going to be an un-happy new year for Dallas Cowboys fans.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed on Monday, Sept. 7 that offensive lineman Tyler Smith will be sidelined for four to six weeks because of thumb surgery.

Smith, the 2023 second-team All-Pro, will have surgery Tuesday to correct an injury to his left thumb, per Schottenheimer. He will be placed on Injured Reserve (IR) with a designation to return. On IR, Smith will have to miss the minimum four games before he can return.

"We know he's a quick healer, and we want to get it fixed and he'll be back before too long," Schottenheimer told reporters Monday.

Smith will be replaced by T.J. Bass, who played in 16 games (five starts) in 2025 for Dallas.

It's an early blow to Dallas, which will play a host of tough defensive teams in the first month-plus of the season, including the Baltimore Ravens, Houston Texans and Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Weeks 3, 4 and 5.

Waiting in Week 6 are the Green Bay Packers, who may return former Cowboy Micah Parsons from injury at that point.

The Cowboys open their 2026 schedule vs. the upstart New York Giants on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 1.

Tyler Smith injury update

The Cowboys' All-Pro left guard was placed on IR with a designation to return, according to head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

Smith was dealing with a thumb injury, but opted to have surgery instead of playing through it. He will miss the minimum four games while on IR, with a return coming in four to six weeks, Schottenheimer said.

item.title: Mike McCarthy hopeful that Joey Porter will play Week 1
item.description: The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts. Thus, time is running out for the team to complete a long-term deal with cornerback Joey Porter.

"It’s a business, and there's definitely business conversations going on," head coach McCarthy said Monday, via Jack Markowski of SI.com.

McCarthy insinuated that he expects Porter to play regardless how talks turn out before Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

"Yeah, I hope so," McCarthy said. "You know, just keep working him. He's still, I'd put him in a ramp-up mode."

When asked what happens if Porter doesn't play, McCarthy said, “We’ll see what happens.”

Porter practiced for the first time last Tuesday after spending all of training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list. But last week he was noncommittal about playing Week 1 absent a contract extension.

Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, is entering the final year of his rookie contract scheduled to make $3.924 million this year.

He is coming off a career year, totaling a career-high 14 passes defensed to go along with 52 tackles, one sack and one interception.

The Lions have filled one of the openings on their active roster.

They announced that they have signed linebacker Joe Bachie off of their practice squad. Bachie spent the offseason and preseason with the team and signed to the practice squad after failing to make the initial 53-man roster in Detroit.

Bachie opened last season with the Colts and started five games before landing on injured reserve. He moved on to the Titans after being released and played in 10 more games on special teams. He finished the year with 29 tackles and had 48 tackles in 51 games for the Bengals and Eagles earlier in his career.

The Lions still have one open spot on the 53-man roster after waiving center Seth McLaughlin and running back Jabari Small last week. They announced that both those players have been signed to the practice squad on Monday.

item.title: Mike Evans downplays missing time: ‘None of my injuries were significant’
item.description: Mike Evans believed he could have practiced in recent weeks had it been a game week
item.content:encoded:
Several members of the San Francisco 49ers returned to practice.

It’s hard to overstate how important defenders like Renardo Green, Romello Height, and Gracen Halton are to the defense. Depth is already at a premium across the board. The pass rush was bleak in 2025. The rookies will play a big role in the defense’s success.

As much as we focus on the rookies on offense, they’ll go as far as Mike Evans takes them. I get the feeling everybody in the building is aware of that, and that’s why the team has been as cautious with Evans since training camp began.

During a recent press conference, Evans downplayed his injuries, saying he would have been on the field had it been a game week:

“The training staff, they did a great job working with me. I know I’m an older player. I’ve had probably over a thousand practices, football practices in my life now, so I know what I’m doing out there. They know what they’re doing. They did a good job taking care of me. None of my injuries were significant. If it was a game week, I wouldn’t have missed any time.”

Evans sustained a groin injury during a preseason practice. He also failed to finish the joint practice against the Chargers, where he was seen with an ice wrap on his left quad.

Evans practicing early in the week will be what we look for all season. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said, “he’s never practiced three days in a row,” so expect Evans to get plenty of veteran days off, much like Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams.

item.title: Dylan Cook trending to start at right tackle for Steelers Week 1
item.description: Mike McCarthy provided an update in the Steelers’ right tackle battle in Monday’s press conference.
item.content:encoded:
When the Pittsburgh Steelers selected Max Iheanachor 21st overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, the immediate question was how soon the young tackle would be thrust into the starting lineup.

It seems as though Steelers fans will have to wait for the regular-season debut of their first-round draft pick, as Dylan Cook appears to be slated to start at right tackle when the Steelers take the field against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.

During his press conference on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy would not commit to naming a definitive starter at right tackle, but he offered some insight into what the team is thinking just days before their Week 1 matchup.

McCarthy said that Cook has been taking “most of the reps” at right tackle as he has been all summer long.

“We feel really good about Dylan,” McCarthy told the media when asked about cohesion among the five starting offensive linemen.

Combine what McCarthy said about Cook taking most of the reps and a vote of confidence, and it’s reasonable to assume that it will be No. 60 getting the nod to start in Week 1.

Later in his media availability, the Steelers head coach expressed how impressed he has been with Iheanachor when he has been healthy enough to play. “Make no mistake about it, he can play,” McCarthy said.

Due to the injury that the rookie tackle suffered in camp, it seems that Iheanchor will have to wait to earn a spot in the starting lineup on Pittsburgh’s offensive line. It would be tough to throw the rookie tackle into the starting lineup right away after playing in just one preseason game, so this seems like the decision we have all been expecting.

The Steelers offensive line will have new starters in Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson to begin 2026. After an up-and-down performance in the preseason, McCarthy is putting his faith in the offensive line to come together ahead of their season opener.

item.title: Steelers won't have full-season captains under Mike McCarthy
item.description: It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains.
item.content:encoded:
It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains. In Pittsburgh, however, there won't be a tweet with anywhere from five to 11 players listed as those who will be wearing a "C" in 2026.

New coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Monday that he won’t use full-season captains. Instead, he'll name captains for each week’s game. That's how McCarthy handled the captain designations while serving as the head coach of the Packers and the Cowboys.

The approach is a clear departure from past practices under Mike Tomlin, and another clear sign that some things will be very different with one Mike yielding to another.

Last year, the Steelers had four permanent captains: quarterback Aaron Rodgers, defensive lineman Cameron Heyward, linebacker T.J. Watt, and safety Miles Killebrew. (After Killebrew was lost for the season due to injury, linebacker Payton Wilson replaced Killebrew as the special-teams captain.)

item.title: ESPN’s models project just 7 wins for the NY Giants
item.description: ESPN predicts yet another losing season for the Giants, but are they setting themselves up for a surprise?
item.content:encoded:
How will the 2026 season play out? Well, nobody really knows.

That, of course, isn’t stopping people from trying to project it. Seth Walder of ESPN released their prediction of how the season will go on Monday. ESPN’s projections are based on their football power index (FPI) and 10,000 simulations of the season.

The average result of those simulations has the New York Giants finishing with a 7-10 record amid season-ending losses to the Cowboys and Eagles.

With two weeks left, the Cowboys, Eagles and Giants were in a three-way tie with mediocre 7-8 records. It took weeks for Philadelphia to find its offensive rhythm under new coordinator Sean Mannion. The Cowboys’ new-look defense held up well early in the season but couldn’t sustain that improvement, causing Dallas to enter the final two weeks on a four-game losing streak. The Giants’ passing game struggled early with wide receiver Malik Nabers being limited but got better as he got healthier.

All three teams had a shot at the playoffs with two games left. The Cowboys dealt a major blow to New York in Week 17, winning a 19-7 defensive battle. The Eagles upset the 49ers 23-19 on the road. But the Cowboys had the tiebreaker advantage, so Dallas took the division when it beat the Commanders in Week 18 even though Philadelphia prevailed over the Giants to finish with an identical 9-8 record.

The playoffs start off with a bang for the Cowboys, with Dak Prescott putting up 31 points on the Seahawks’ defense, while limiting Seattle to just 19. They come crashing back to Earth the next week and are ejected from the dance by the Detroit Lions.

Chris’ thoughts

Could this scenario come to pass? Well, obviously, anything can happen. However I think I’d be pretty stunned if this exact scenario played out — and probably nowhere near as stunned as the folks at ESPN would be if their prediction came true.

I’m not surprised that ESPN’s models are pretty low on the NFC East. After all, the division was weak last year, and these models tend to be rear-looking. However, the division also abounds with new coordinators and schemes and nobody quite knows how the various units will perform under their new coaches.

The Cowboys are widely expected to make a leap thanks to the arrival of new DC Christian Parker and rookie S Caleb Downs. However, Downs is in fact a rookie, and there’s always a learning curve with rookies. Likewise, while Parker is a Vic Fangio disicple and has been hailed as a wunderkind, he has never run an NFL defense before. There’s no way to definitively say whether he will be a success or not.

Likewise, Sean Manion has never run an NFL offense and the Eagles will be without A.J. Brown. The Eagles have been more efficient and explosive with Green than without him, and we don’t know if Dontavian Wicks will be able to fill Brown’s shoes or how Jalen Hurts will adapt to his new reality.

And finally, the Washington Commanders may be planning to ape Brian Flores’ blitz-happy approach to mask their defensive limitations. Will they? And if they do, will it work? And can Jayden Daniels stay healthy for the full season and return to his rookie form?

The Giants, as we’ve covered extensively, have completely retooled their offense and defense. Nobody is quite surewhat the former will look like under Matt Nagy, Brian Callahan, and Greg Roman. It is interesting that the media is so high on rookie coaches like Parker and Manion, while dismissing the Giants’ own experienced coaching staff. I’ll admit my bias in being optimistic for the Giants this year. But (as I’ve written before) it seems odd to me that so many are predicting that the best the Giants can do is win the same number of games they should have won the year before. And with what is expected to be a stronger roster and far better coaching, at that.

The good news is that we’ll get the answers to all these questions soon, as opening day is rapidly approaching. But for now, it’s still fun to speculate as we pass the time.

item.title: Patriots-Christian Gonzalez contract negotiations reportedly ‘nowhere’
item.description: A deal being reached before the regular season seems increasingly unlikely.
item.content:encoded:
With the NFL season opener approaching fast, the New England Patriots and their best defender, cornerback Christian Gonzalez, have yet to reach common ground in their contract negotiations. In fact, it seems that the two sides remain significantly apart.

Appearing on ESPN’s Pat McAfee Show on Monday, NFL insider Adam Schefter painted a bleak picture.

“These things always can change. But as of right now, talks are nowhere,” he said.

“There always can be a last-second push and there always can be something that changes,” Schefter continued. “We’ll see how the two sides address it once the season’s underway. But I think, as of right now, it’s hard to imagine that the two sides would be able to make up the difference to get a deal done by opening night. We’ve seen crazy things happen, and I’m sure there could be another push to try to see if they could salvage it and get it done. But right now, as of yesterday, I was told it was not close. We’ll see if they can figure out anything by the start of the game. It didn’t sound like that was going to be the case.”

The Patriots’ first-round draft pick in 2023, Gonzalez has been one of the NFL’s top cornerbacks since entering the league. As a result, the 24-year-old is looking to become the league’s highest-paid player in the league at his position — something the organization, by its own admission, is willing to support.

At the moment, that title belongs to Devon Witherspoon. A fellow 2023 draft pick, Witherspoon signed a four-year, $132 million extension with the Seattle Seahawks earlier this offseason. In terms of average annual value ($33M) and total guarantees ($101M), no cornerback has ever been above the three-time Pro Bowler.

Gonzalez, according to Schefter, is looking to at least match Witherspoon. However, the Patriots — despite statements to the contrary by both team owner Robert Kraft and de facto general manager Eliot Wolf — apparently “have never been there” and “have not gotten close to there.”

Time will tell how accurate that information is, and whether or not the Patriots will reach a common ground after all. There is at least one NFL insider, though, who thinks so: Benjamin Allbright of KOA Colorado posted on Sunday that a “deal eventually will get done.”

item.title: Cowboys starting left guard Tyler Smith out 4-6 weeks with thumb injury
item.description: The Cowboys are going to be without Tyler Smith for some time.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys starting left guard Tyler Smith was not on the field for the team’s practice on Monday afternoon, and unfortunately we now know why. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced after the practice that Smith will need thumb surgery, and is expected to miss four to six weeks.

We got further confirmation that this has been bothering Smith for a while and that they tried to avoid surgery, but were ultimately unsuccessful. T.J. Bass will get his opportunity to step in.

Interior offensive line depth was one of the biggest concerns for the Cowboys all training camp and preseason, and now right off the bat they’ve been dealt the biggest possible blow, losing the experienced Smith at left guard. Luckily Bass is the backup with the most experience capable of stepping into this spot, and Dallas also has Ajani Cornelius as they prepare for week one on Sunday night at the Giants.

item.title: Monken doesn't rule out Browns using rookie QB in offensive 'package' Week 1 at Jaguars
item.description: It wouldn't be surprising if the Cleveland Browns played multiple quarterbacks this season. In fact, they could even do that in Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
It wouldn't be surprising if the Cleveland Browns played multiple quarterbacks this season. In fact, they could even do that in Week 1.

Browns head coach Todd Monken named Deshaun Watson the starter and Shedeur Sanders the backup for the team's Week 1 game at the Jacksonville Jaguars (1 p.m. ET, CBS). But when asked Monday whether third-string QB Taylen Green also could be active, Monken suggested it was a possibility.

"Could be," Monken said. "There could be a package where we have him."

Monken also admitted that "three is a lot" when it comes to rostering quarterbacks. If the Browns wanted to use Green against the Jaguars but also have Sanders ready to replace Watson in case of injury or ineffectiveness, they'd have to make all three active and essentially take an active spot away from another player. They wouldn't be able to use the emergency third QB spot in that situation.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Green, the Browns' sixth-round pick this April out of Arkansas, earned his spot on the roster when the team placed Dillon Gabriel on injured reserve with a back injury prior to roster cutdowns. At 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Green is an athletically blessed QB with plus running ability. 

His NFL scouting combine workout was a pretty good snapshot of that rare athleticism. Green clocked a 4.36-second 40-yard dash, which was the fastest by a true quarterback in more than 20 years and also registered eye-opening numbers in the vertical jump (43 1/2 inches) and broad jump (11 feet, 2 inches).

In 2025 for the Razorbacks, Green rushed 139 times for 777 yards (5.6-yard average) and eight scores. In four college seasons with Boise State and Arkansas, Green totaled 2,405 rush yards and 35 scores.

Green's running ability was on display in the Browns' preseason finale at New England when he ran eight times for 66 yards (including a 30-yard gallop), also throwing for 27 yards on 5-of-7 passing.

After the game, Monken called Green "a tremendous athlete" and "highly intelligent."

"You saw it," Monken said. "There's a lot to work with there. We've just got to refine it."

When naming Watson the starter on Aug. 24, Monken indicated that Sanders and Green would each split practice reps as the Browns' scout-team quarterbacks as a way of accelerating both in their developments. It was a dramatic increase in activity for Green, who routinely was the fourth QB option in training-camp drills and didn't see action in the first two preseason outings. 

Perhaps this is gamesmanship, giving the Jaguars another thing to think about. Or it could be a sign that Green has been progressing enough to potentially supplant Sanders at some point as the QB2. Either way, the Browns' season-long quarterback plans don't yet appear to be written in stone.

item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin Badgers suffered a blowout 41-13 loss at the hands of the No. 4 Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Sunday evening, as they struggled in the second half of a game that quickly got away from them.

It was a night when the Badgers played many new faces on offense, including quarterback Colton Joseph, as Wisconsin had nine new starters on offense. Who all played, and what was the snap distribution at every position?

Let’s break down Wisconsin’s snap counts and PFF grades and what they mean for the offense.

Colton Joseph – Snap Count: [61], Grade: 57.1

No surprises here. Colton Joseph got all 61 snaps with the offense, as the Badgers kept their starters out there for the whole night despite the blowout.

Abu Sama was the clear lead back with carries, getting 15 to Darrion Dupree’s four. But the two actually got a similar number of snaps, with Dupree coming in on passing downs. The Badgers trust Dupree’s improved pass protection, and he’s the better pass-catcher, keeping Sama fresh with a near-even split.

Chris Brooks, Tyrell Henry, and Malachi Coleman were the clear top three receivers, with Wisconsin interchanging guys from the outside and the slot. Eugene Hilton, despite being listed as a starter, got only 17 reps, while Shamar Rigby got 15 as well. This seems to be Wisconsin’s top five right now.

Coleman was the highlight of the group, catching four passes for 76 yards, while Hilton, Brooks, and Henry caught four, three, and three passes, respectively, as well.

The target distribution was quite even. Henry had seven, Brooks had six, Coleman had five, and Hilton had four.

Bork was the main tight end in bigger sets, as him and Stec got most of the run-blocking reps. Harris saw 17 reps, running a route on over two-thirds of them. Ryan Schwendeman was brought in purely as a blocker for his five reps.

Lucas Simmons-Johansson also got in a little bit at left tackle.

The right guard backup battle left a lot to be desired. That was the position that struggled the most on the offensive line, although Wilkins had some tough moments as well.

Overall, I thought the offensive line honestly wasn’t bad, aside from right guard and a very few select plays (like Colton Joseph’s interception when Wilkins was easily beaten). Blake Cherry and Kevin Heywood gave up two pressures each, per PFF, while Stylz Blackmon, Wilkins, and Colin Cubberly each had one pressure.

Have more coming later, but I thought Cubberly and Austin Kawecki were the two most impressive of the group on Sunday.

item.title: Tua Tagovailoa's return to Pittsburgh puts extra pressure on Mike McCarthy's debut
item.description: The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins. He was benched after the 28-15 loss on a Monday night in December — and he was cut in March.

Fast forward to September, and Tua will be returning to Pittsburgh as the Week 1 starter for the Falcons.

If it goes poorly, Tua may not be starting for very long. If it goes well, and if the Falcons upset the Steelers (Pittsburgh is currently favored by 3.5 points), there will be a very strong reaction in Western Pennsylvania.

Losing to Tua after drubbing him less than nine months earlier will provide the first clear apples-to-apples comparison between new coach Mike McCarthy and his predecessor, Mike Tomlin. Nuances will easily be lost on Steelers Nation. Yes, the Falcons are an overall better team than the 2025 Dolphins. The common denominator is the quarterback; if he plays dramatically better than he did the last time he played in Pittsburgh, Steelers fans will interpret that as an indication that the new boss won't have the same kind of success as the old boss.

It would be dubbed an overreaction. But that's what football fans do. With only seventeen games in a season, they all count. They all spark a reaction. And, at some point, the trend of overreacting shows that, actually, it's the normal and usual reaction to a team losing a game it should have won.

The Steelers have more than a few winnable games in the eight weeks before the bye, including two against the Browns. Anything less than 5-3 will spark high anxiety on and after Week 10, where the Eagles, Broncos, Texans, Jaguars, a road game at the Bengals, and two games against the Ravens are lurking.

The fans who show up in six days will be expecting a 1-0 start. If the end result is 0-1, sphincters will be tightening quickly in the Steel City.

item.title: Matt Suhey, member of Super Bowl-winning '85 Bears and lead blocker for Walter Payton, dies at 68
item.description: Matt Suhey helped Walter Payton finish his career as the NFL's leading rusher.
item.content:encoded:
Matt Suhey, the man responsible for opening holes for Chicago Bears legend Walter Payton, died over the weekend, per multiple reports. He was 68.

Selected by the Bears in the second round of the 1980 NFL Draft, Suhey — a fullback — was brought in to make sure Payton continued to excel as a runner. Both men were extremely successful in that pursuit.

Payton, who was already on a Hall of Fame trajectory, rushed for 9,800 yards and 51 touchdowns in the eight years in which he ran behind Suhey. Following Payton's retirement, Suhey blocked for Neal Anderson, who gained over 1,100 yards running behind Suhey in 1988.

While Suhey was mostly known for his toughness and blocking ability, he did carve out a role as a secondary runner to Payton, getting over 100 carries in four of his 10 NFL seasons.

He finished his career with 2,946 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns. He also played a key role in the 1985 Bears winning the Super Bowl. In the team's three playoff games, he carried the ball 23 times, picking up seven first downs. He also scored a touchdown against the New England Patriots in the Super Bowl.

Prior to his time in Chicago, Suhey starred at Penn State, where he racked up 2,818 rushing yards and 26 touchdowns in his four years with the program.

Though he was a beloved and well-known figure among Bears fans, Suhey was arguably more well known for his relationship with Payton away from the field. The two grew so close that Payton was reportedly the godfather to Suhey's son, per USA Today. Payton's son, Jarrett, has referred to Suhey as a "father figure" after Payton died in 1999, per the Chicago Tribune. During Payton's episode of "A Football Life," Suhey was described as Payton's "best friend."

During that episode, Jarrett perfectly summed up Suhey's relationship with Walter both on and off the field.

"Matt watched my dad's back, kinda like being a bodyguard or protector. He blocked for him. He took a lot of hits. Making sure my dad would get the glory. And Matt kinda just sat around in the background. Very unselfish."

Jarrett also posted a tribute to Suhey on Monday, making some of those very same points.

Matt Suhey passed away yesterday.
He was my dad’s closest friend. After we lost my dad in 1999, Matt became the biggest father figure I had. When everything felt uncertain, he was there. My dad left him in charge and Matt never let that responsibility sit lightly. He protected… pic.twitter.com/pN0I8zDTTz

— Jarrett Payton (@paytonsun) September 7, 2026

Suhey's personality made him a popular player on those '80s Bears teams. When it came time for Bears lineman Jimbo Covert to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, he chose Suhey as his presenter for the event.

item.title: What does Darrell Luter Jr. bring to Las Vegas Raiders’ roster?
item.description: Breaking down the new CB’s tape
item.content:encoded:
Even after the Las Vegas Raiders filled out their initial 53-man roster at the end of training camp, John Spytek and Klint Kubiak weren’t done making one last tweak. The Raiders picked up cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. from the San Francisco 49ers off the waiver wire, who drew the most interest on the wire with four other teams putting a claim in on him, according to ESPN’s Field Yates.

Luter is expected to serve as a backup corner and special teamer on the Raiders’ roster. He was a key specialist in San Francisco, recording over 500 career snaps on special teams over the last three years by contributing to every unit except for the field goal/PAT kicking team, according to Pro Football Focus. Last season, the 2023 fifth-round pick recorded six total tackles and earned a 68.9 special teams grade.

Defensively, the four-year pro doesn’t have much regular-season experience with 342 career snaps, 275 of them and all three of his career starts coming last season. He was targeted 18 times in 2025 and yielded 12 catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns with one PBU, per PFF.

However, Luter drew interest with a strong performance in the preseason this summer, allowing just two catches for 18 yards and no touchdowns (one PBU) on seven targets, per PFF. With that in mind, let’s dive into the last three games and see what the veteran corner can bring to Las Vegas’ defense.

I’ll dive deeper into a few of the reps, but above is a look at every time Luter was targeted during the 2026 preseason. If you’re keeping score at home, there are eight plays up there. The discrepency in the targets appears to be that PFF has the linebacker drawing the target on Fernando Mendoza’s interception above.

The biggest area of improvement that stands out is his change of direction, as he often has a hitch in his transitions and struggles to drive on routes. However, the Southern Alabama product has decent ball skills and can be effective in press coverage, which lines up with Lance Zierlein of NFL.com’s scouting report when Luter was a draft prospect.

“Long-limbed (32 3/8-inch arms) press-cover cornerback with the ball skills and physicality to challenge receivers outside the numbers,” Zierlein wrote. “Luter can be a little leggy in his transitions and burst to the football, but his length helps make up for that and creates pass breakups. Louisiana-Monroe attacked him with back-shoulder throws all game, which is something to keep an eye on in the pros. He’s going to be more effective in press-and-shadow coverage than he is playing Cover 3 or off-man. His ball production dipped in 2022, but his length and playing style fit the NFL game.”

For the record, the former Jaguar had four interceptions and 10 passes defended in 2021 before racking up one pick and seven PDs in 2022.

This rep provides a 1,000-foot view of Luter’s strengths and weaknesses.

He’s playing off-coverage and is isolated against the single receiver in the three-by-one formation. The wideout runs an out route, and the corner does a good job of staying on top of it. Then, the latter has a hitch when trying to drive on the route, which prevents him from being in position to make a play on the ball as it arrives. However, he does have enough speed to get back in the picture after the receiver bobbles the catch, allowing Luter to play the wideout’s hands and prevent the completion.

So, the change-of-direction skills are subpar to give his man an opportunity to make the catch. But Luter’s straight-line speed and long arms allow him to take advantage of a mistake and end up winning the rep. For those curious, he ran a 4.46-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine three years ago.

As Zierlein noted, Luter is at his best in press coverage, and this is a good example of what he can do when he gets his hands on receivers.

Luter starts the play as if he’s in soft-shoe coverage (press without a jam) but times up his jam/punch to make contact about four yards into the five-yard window. That’s a good change-up because it can catch wide receivers off-guard, where they’re thinking that they won’t have to deal with any physicality since there was no jam at the line of scrimmage.

Additionally, that disrupts the timing of the route, and the corner does a good job of squeezing the wideout toward the sideline to give the quarterback less room to complete the pass to the go route. From there, Luter is in-phase throughout the route, staying in the receiver’s hip pocket. So, he can turn his head to locate the ball in the air and make a play on it instead of nearly overrunning the under throw.

But, at the end of the day, Luter has tight coverage and does his job by breaking up the pass. Just with his backside instead of his hands!

You might remember watching this rep during the preseason, as Luter makes a nice play against his new teammates Malik Benson and Fernando Mendoza.

This rep is pretty similar to the last one, only he stays in soft-shoe coverage against the go/fade route this time. Also, he does a better job of turning his head to find the ball in the air to be in perfect position to defend against the back-shoulder throw. Those long arms come in handy at the catch point, as he’s able to come up with a PBU to finish the rep and put the Raiders in a third-and-long situation.

The fourth-year pro is also a pretty good tackler, which is another area where his long arms come into play, and the clip above is a great example.

It looks like the 49ers are running Cover 3 with pattern matching principles since both corners have their eyes on the wide receivers they’re lined up across from, while the underneath defenders fall into their zones post-snap. Meanwhile, the Raiders have a good play design where the receiver lined up across from Luter runs a crossing route to get the corner out of position to defend the screen.

However, Luter recognizes the play design and crashes downhill. He does benefit from left tackle Kolton Miller eyeing the linebackers and being late to see the corner outside. But Luter’s speed and long arms allow him to take advantage by using a good angle and laying out to trip up Michael Mayer for a one-yard gain.

That’s a heads-up play, in addition to the speed and tackling skills.

We’ll wrap up here with a nice play in run support, which is a big part of Luter’s game. For example, he posted an 82.0 PFF run defense grade during the regular season last year, and has had marks of 81.4 and 81.6 during the last two respective preseasons.

He’s in off coverage in the boundary, as it appears that San Francisco had either Cover 1 or 3 called out of a two-high look pre-snap, meaning the boundary safety rotates down into the box. Once Luter recognizes the receiver he’s lined up across from goes to crack block said safety, he transitions downhill and starts pursuing to the football.

The corner’s speed becomes a factor, again, allowing him to make a clean-up tackle for a one-yard gain after the linebacker missed. This may not seem like much, but it’s excellent run support from a defensive back who started the play about nine yards away from the line of scrimmage. If Luter isn’t there, this is at least a gain that puts the offense ahead of schedule and might even be a first down.

It will be interesting to see what the coaching staff’s plan is for the waiver wire pickup. His subpar change of direction and short-area quickness can create some issues in coverage, but he does have intriguing natural gifts with his arm length, speed and press coverage skills. Luter doesn’t have much experience playing either of these positions, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he gets a shot at nickel and/or safety with how good of a tackler he is. Of course, all of this is in addition to what he brings on special teams.
